correctness.rationale: Normalize c and ε by row translation, which multiplies each column by a nonzero phase, and put z_y=ζ_p^(ay). For homogeneous parity the two center rows are proportional, while any three projected columns have a nonsingular three-row minor with rows 1,z_y,z_y^(−1), by a column-scaled Vandermonde. For 3+1 the sum/difference of the center rows isolates the singleton, leaving the same Vandermonde on the other three columns. For 2+2, block differences reduce rank to 2+rank K: the two first coordinates of K are nonzero z-differences, and its second coordinate in each column is its first multiplied by −1/(z_u z_v) for that pair. Thus rank is exactly three iff the pair sums agree modulo p, otherwise four. In a balanced partner two columns of opposite parity are distinguished by the center-row ratio and two same-parity columns by the 0-to-a phase ratio; similarly the two center rows differ across parity, and rows at distinct projected coordinates have different ratios on the two columns of either parity. Homogeneous partners always have proportional center rows. The pair counts are ((p−1)/2)² per common sum, with p choices of sum and 2 binom(p,4) additional homogeneous partners; p=3 is included with none of the latter. The repeated projected residue and majority parity recover c and ε, and the remaining unordered offsets give (p−1)/2 choices. Analytic replay: frozen RESULT.md lines 32–59. The checker was inspected but not executed: it certifies determinants at finitely many primes via cyclotomic arithmetic and tests proportionality, not the all-prime theorem nor exact lower ranks by itself.
